findings.title: Unstable cache key built with Python hash()
findings.body: Line 27 builds the cache key with hash(tuple(sorted(snuba_params.project_ids))). Python's hash() for tuples is salted per-process (PYTHONHASHSEED), so the same project set maps to different keys in different workers/restarts, defeating the shared cache and causing inconsistent behavior. It can also be negative and can collide. Use a stable deterministic encoding such as comma-joined sorted ids instead.

findings.title: Stale allowlist cache returns wrong counts with no invalidation
findings.body: is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects caches allowlist eligibility for 60s and invalidate_upsampling_cache is defined but never called. A stale True applies sum(sample_weight) (~10x inflation) to projects just removed from the allowlist; a stale False under-counts projects just added. Count correctness must not depend on eventual consistency for a global option lookup.

findings.title: Upsampling check uses outer dataset instead of scoped_dataset
findings.body: _get_event_stats takes scoped_dataset (which the dashboard-split factory changes to discover vs the original dataset) but calls is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects with the outer closure variable dataset. After a split decision the eligibility decision and column transform are therefore made for the wrong dataset, applying upsampling to transaction-like queries or skipping it for error queries.

findings.title: upsampled_count sums nullable sample_weight and truncates with toInt64
findings.body: upsampled_count is defined as toInt64(sum(sample_weight)) with no coalesce/default. Rows without sample_weight contribute NULL/0 and are silently dropped from the count, under-counting mixed data, and toInt64 truncates fractional weights (e.g. 1/0.3). The helper even states it assumes the column always exists. Use coalesce/ifNull handling and avoid lossy integer truncation.

findings.title: Discover error detection misses negated/default error queries
findings.body: _is_error_focused_query only returns True when the literal string event.type:error appears. The same file's caller and the dashboard-split code issue error queries as (query) AND !event.type:transaction and empty/default queries, which will therefore skip upsampling on discover while the errors dataset upsamples, producing inconsistent under-counts.

findings.title: Sample-rate test helper swallows errors and mishandles falsy/invalid rates
findings.body: In _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling the lookups and float conversion are wrapped in bare except Exception: pass and gated by if client_sample_rate:. This hides malformed contexts, treats 0/0.0 as absent, and accepts out-of-range values like >1 or negative, writing a bad sample_rate into normalized_data that then drives sample_weight in tests.
